title: Grab a Meta Quest 3S With Golf+ for Under $300 at Amazon Now for Black Friday
summary: It's a great option if you're looking to get into VR, or want to upgrade an old headset.
content: If you've been out of the VR scene for a minute, you might not realize just how many competitive standalone headsets there are nowadays. Between the highly sought-after Valve Steam Frame , the recently announced Meta VR Glasses , and the lineup of Meta Quest headsets , there's quite a spectrum to choose from depending on your needs. The Meta Quest 3S, released in 2024, is still the latest headset from Meta, taking over as the new entry-level headset following the discontinuation of the Meta Quest 2. It's a great option if you're looking to get into VR, or want to upgrade an old headset. Even better, it's currently on sale for 15% off the regular price as part of Amazon's Black Friday sale . Check out the full rundown below for more details. Meta Quest 3S Bundle for $297 The Meta Quest 3S is a blend between the current flagship Meta Quest 3 and the previous generation Meta Quest 2, offering a great entry into VR for just about anyone. The Quest 3S features the same Snapdragon XR2 Gen 2 chip with 8GB RAM as the Quest 3, allowing you to play any modern VR game without issues. As a way to reduce the overall cost a bit, the Quest 3S features a lower resolution display (the same as the Quest 2, in fact) and uses the older Fresnel lenses, which make the headset slightly bulkier than that of the Quest 3. However, it does allow for full-color passthrough, making this a great mixed reality headset. While Meta has a number of Black Friday bundles available for the Quest 3S, the absolute lowest price option available is $297 for the 128GB model, which also includes Golf+ (a $30 value) and 1,800 in-game credits (a $10 value) which can be used to purchase additional courses. This deal is available now through November 30 and is likely the best discount we'll see for the rest of 2026.

title: GTA 6 Animation Director Reveals Rockstar Made 3 Animations for Each Item Interaction
summary: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game.
content: Mike Jones, the director of gameplay animation for GTA 6, revealed that the team at Rockstar created three separate animations for each item interaction in the game. If you’ve been playing GTA 6 at all, you’ve probably picked up on the fact that characters can now hold an item in each hand. This has made for some especially funny clips on social media, where users have wasted no time making Jason recreate the ‘six-seven’ meme while holding various objects. This is a big change from previous Rockstar games; in titles like GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 , players could only carry one thing at a time, though you could dual wield certain guns in GTA: San Andreas. (You could also hold longarms at your side while shooting a pistol in RDR 2 and Max Payne 3 .) Now, you can hold a sandwich in one hand and a drink in the other — or a bag and a gun, if you’re sticking up a pawn shop, for instance. This isn’t just an aesthetic feature, either, as it serves the important function of letting players take care of two tasks at once, making robberies or transporting items a bit smoother. Players have praised GTA 6 for its jaw-dropping attention to detail, and this particular tidbit wasn’t lost on them. A thread on Bluesky discussing the feature caught the attention of Mike Jones, the director of gameplay on Rockstar’s latest title, who revealed the extent of the studio’s efforts in making sure every single item interaction had a single-handed, two-handed, and hands-free animations. “FYI, we made three versions for all item interactions; one if both hands are free, one if just your right hand is free and again for the left,” he wrote . “It was a massive pain, but once you knew every interaction could ‘cope,’ it made the game logic much easier. That was then sometimes replicated for crouch, too…” That being said, the devs at Rockstar aren’t superheroes, and they had to cut corners somewhere during development. Jones admitted this fact in response to another comment in this thread, where a user wrote, “Honestly, the level of polish is so absurd that when I see how cheated the ‘putting gas in the car’ sequence is, I'm like, relieved. ‘Oh, okay, they're human, they bleed.’ You all did SO well.” “Thanks, everyone would really appreciate your comments! And yes, shortcuts were definitely made, too,” Jones replied. GTA 6 is a game like no other. Its world is so massive and detailed that some players are avoiding progressing the story in favor of chilling out in Key Lento and diving for treasure, fishing with Cal, and playing billiards at the Rusty Anchor. title: GTA 6 Doesn't Let You Replay Missions, and Rockstar Says There's a Good Reason for That
summary: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar.
content: GTA 6 gives players a lot of freedom in how the story and quests play out, but it came at the cost of letting players replay missions, according to Rockstar. When speaking with Kotaku , Rockstar Games senior design director Scott Butchard explained why the studio scrapped a mission replay menu in GTA 6. Both GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 allowed players to freely replay missions, but that's not the case in GTA 6 . According to Butchard, they considered bringing the feature back, but cut it because it was "at odds" with the story. “Mission replay was certainly something we looked at early on in development, and we do not currently support it,” said Butchard. “As the game came together it felt at odds with the story we were trying to tell and felt a bit alien and disconnected. Sitting outside of the game as it were and replaying missions really diminished the choices you had made.” The lack of a mission replay option has been a point of contention for fans. GTA 6 has some of the best missions in the franchise, particularly the final mission of Chapter 1. Given that GTA 6 can take players anywhere from 50 - 100 hours to finish, most people probably won't start the entire game over just to re-experience their favorite mission. However, it's worth noting that Butchard says the game doesn't "currently support" this feature. Maybe it'll come in the form of an update later, but Rockstar hasn't confirmed that. GTA 6's story and missions can deviate somewhat significantly based on your choices. Certain characters can be killed or spared, objectives can be completed in different ways, and the entire relationship between Jason and Lucia can vary based on your actions. You can get entirely different dialogue options and cutscenes based on these differences, which might be why a mission replay system isn't as straightforward as it was previous games. However, Red Dead Redemption 2 also featured different choices that changed Arthur's character. It wasn't quite as nuanced as GTA 6's variations, though. Maybe Rockstar will figure out a way to do this, but it clearly fell low on the priority list, if it was on the list at all by the end of development. Even if Rockstar never adds it, modders will probably find a way to slot it in when the inevitable PC version releases. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? title: Spotify Reveals Massive Spike in Streams for Music Featured in GTA 6
summary: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6, including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago.
content: Spotify has released new data that shows huge spikes in streams for music featured in GTA 6 , including a Carly Rae Jepsen song from over a decade ago. In an email sent to IGN, Spotify revealed that the GTA 6 hype is inspiring listeners to add tons of music from the game to their playlists. In addition to hype for the original music created specifically for the game, such as Justice's Flower in a Hurricane, Carly Rae Jepsen's 2015 song Run Away With Me saw a 940% increase in streams following the game's release. The song plays during a pivotal moment in GTA 6's first chapter and is arguably one of the best sections in the game. Additionally, fans are listening to the official GTA 6 playlist en masse and are actively searching for things related to the game. You can view the full breakdown courtesy of Spotify below. Following the release of GTA 6, streams of Carly Rae Jepsen's “Run Away With Me” spiked on Nov. 24, increasing by 940% in the U.S. and 1,255% in Canada compared to its average streams. On Nov. 23, “Flower In A Hurricane” by Justice, Tame Impala, SZA and King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard hit number 1 on BOTH Spotify’s Daily Top Songs charts globally and in the U.S. Streams of The Official Grand Theft Auto Playlist surged week over week, rising 275% globally and 355% in the U.S. (on Nov. 19 as compared to Nov. 12). GTA had fans searching for more. Searches containing “GTA,” “GTA6/VI” or “Grand Theft Auto” surged about 510% globally and 600% in the U.S. compared with the week prior (Nov. 19 vs. Nov. 12). GTA 6 has been shattering all kinds of records and setting new trends. The game had the biggest launch in the history of PlayStation and sold nearly $4 billion worth of copies in its first 24 hours , making it the highest-grossing entertainment launch of all time by a significant margin. The game has also set viewership records on platforms like Twitch , led to a massive increase in internet traffic , and so much more. It's a massive cultural moment that's likely not going to end anytime soon. Not only will this game likely get bigger, but it also has more big events on the horizon. It's also expected to release on PC early next year, and an online mode is also heavily speculated to come in the future. Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next?
